text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

Abstract  
GSE309890 is a gene expression study deposited in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) that investigates how the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor sertraline affects antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli. The study demonstrates that sertraline biases resistance emergence by triggering metabolic shifts—in particular, redirecting glucose metabolism from glycolysis to the pentose phosphate pathway via activation of transketolase A. The series involves expression profiling by high throughput sequencing from six samples, comparing adaptive evolving cultures against controls. Supplementary files hosted on the GEO FTP server provide processed expression data in CSV format. This result matters because it elucidates a potential modifiable metabolic trait that could be targeted to restore antibiotic sensitivity, thereby mitigating sertraline-induced resistance. The study is detailed in the GEO Series record using data from E. coli strain K-12 substr. MG1655 and is linked to a BioProject. These points underline the significance of metabolic rewiring in antibiotic resistance mechanisms.

I. Introduction  
Background. GSE309890 examines the impact of sertraline on antibiotic resistance in E. coli. The study uses expression profiling to characterize metabolic shifts, specifically the role of the pentose phosphate pathway and the enzyme transketolase A (tktA), in mediating resistance.  
Literature Review. No linked PubMed reference exists in the GEO record, suggesting the study may be unpublished or pending indexing.  
Knowledge Gap. Prior to this study, the metabolic consequences of SSRI exposure on bacterial resistance were not well understood.  
Objective & Hypothesis. The study aims to demonstrate that sertraline exposure forces a metabolic shift in E. coli that biases mutations toward resistance, and that targeting tktA can reverse this effect.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. The GEO Series record provides details on the experimental design and sample setup with three replicates for adaptive evolution and three controls.  
Materials. The dataset includes RNA-seq derived expression data for E. coli (strain K-12 substr. MG1655) using platform GPL24659.  
Procedures. The study’s processed expression values were compressed as a CSV (.csv.gz) file, available via the GEO FTP tree.  
Statistical Analysis. Although detailed statistical methods are not embedded in the GEO record, the supplementary files are expected to contain normalized metrics such as FPKMs.

III. Results  
Data Presentation. The key attributes of GSE309890 are summarized in Table 1.

Table 1. Summary of GSE309890  
---------------------------------------------------------------
Attribute                        | Detail  
---------------------------------------------------------------
Title                            | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback  
Summary                          | Study demonstrating sertraline-induced metabolic rewiring leading to biased antibiotic resistance in E. coli  
Organism                         | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655  
Experiment Type                  | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing  
Sample Count                     | 6 (3 adaptive evolution replicates, 3 controls)  
Supplementary File Available     | GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz  
FTP Directory URL                | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/  
---------------------------------------------------------------

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The GEO record confirms that the study centers on sertraline-induced metabolic changes that facilitate resistance through alterations in the pentose phosphate pathway. The availability of a single supplementary file containing FPKM values enables downstream analysis of expression profiles.  
Context. The experimental design using adaptive evolution versus control samples shows a clear approach to isolating the effect of sertraline, though the absence of a PubMed record leaves external validation pending.  
Limitations. The record does not include raw sequencing files or detailed metadata beyond the supplementary CSV file, and processed data is limited to the provided file.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 underscores the metabolic basis of resistance emergence under sertraline exposure. Future queries may focus on detailed statistical analyses or complementary proteomic data to further validate the metabolic rollback hypothesis.

References  
[1] GEO Series GSE309890 Record URL: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO FTP Directory URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/

Acknowledgments  
We acknowledge the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) for providing the dataset and supplementary file access.
